wording_verbatim: Have you ever used ChatGPT for any of the following? — For entertainment / To learn something new / For tasks at work
base_population: US adults who have heard at least a little about ChatGPT (GPT1); in Mar 2023 the battery was the survey's only usage measure; Form 2 half-sample from Jul 2023
response_options: Yes, I have done this / No, I have not done this
break_note: Mar 2023 wave had no direct use question; the published 14% is the combined any-of-three figure. Topline footnote: "In March 2023, GPT2 did not use a randomly assigned split form."

wording_verbatim: Have you ever used ChatGPT for any of the following? — For tasks at work
base_population: US adults who have heard at least a little about ChatGPT AND are currently working for pay
response_options: Yes, I have done this / No, I have not done this
break_note: Work item of the GPT2 battery; replaced in 2026 by the chatbot-category CHATWHY2 work item (different construct and base).

base_population: US adults who have heard at least a little about ChatGPT (Form 1 half-sample); Pew re-based prior waves to all adults in 2025/2026 trend tables
response_options: Yes, I have done this / No, I have not done this
break_note: Retired after Feb/Mar 2025. W187 footnote 3: "Prior to 2026, this question was asked among those who had heard at least a little about ChatGPT. It is presented here among all adults, accounting for form splits in previous surveys."

wording_verbatim: Have you ever used an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot like ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot?
base_population: US adults who heard at least a little about AI chatbots (re-based to all adults in the 2026 topline)
response_options: Yes, I have / No, I have not
break_note: Single fielding (Aug 2024). Successor changed "Have you ever used" to "Do you ever use" (ever-use vs current-use) and asked all adults — not wording-comparable despite Pew presenting it as trend-for-comparison.

wording_verbatim: Do you ever use an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot like ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot?
base_population: All US adults
response_options: Yes, I do / No, I do not
break_note: 2026 redesign: chatbot-category current-use item asked of all adults replaces both the ChatGPT-specific GPTUSE series and the 2024 ever-use bridge.

wording_verbatim: Which of the following artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots do you ever use?
base_population: All US adults; ChatGPT asked of all, Claude/Copilot/Character.ai Form 1 (N=2,555), Gemini/Meta AI/Grok Form 2 (N=2,564)
response_options: Yes, I use this / No, I do not use this
break_note: Brand checklist; per-brand estimates are separate rows (brand named in notes).

wording_verbatim: About how often do you use an artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot like ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot?
base_population: US adults who use AI chatbots (CHATUSEMOD=1, N=2,605); topline also re-bases to all adults
response_options: Almost constantly / Several times a day / About once a day / Several times a week / Less often

wording_verbatim: Do you ever use artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for the following? — For tasks at work
base_population: AI-chatbot users currently working for pay (N=1,894); topline also re-bases to all employed adults (N=3,038)
response_options: Yes, I do / No, I do not
break_note: Successor to the ChatGPT-specific GPT2 work item; chatbot-category, different base.

wording_verbatim: Just your impression, how often do you interact with artificial intelligence (AI)?
base_population: All US adults
response_options: Almost constantly / Several times a day / About once a day / Several times a week / Less often
break_note: Perceived ambient interaction, not tool adoption — kept because it is Pew's longest-running AI-use frequency trend; no single headline share published (distribution-only rows).

wording_verbatim: Now thinking of the tasks you do in your job, how much of your work is done with AI?
base_population: Employed US adults with one job or a primary job who have heard at least a little about AI in the workplace (AIWRKHEARD gate)
response_options: All of it / Most of it / Some of it / Not much of it / None of it / Not sure
break_note: Preceded by AIWRKHEARD framing item; published headline is the combined All+Most+Some share.

publisher_definition: Gallup defines "Total AI users" as employees who say they used AI at work a few times a year or more.
base_population: US adults 18+ working full or part time for organizations, Gallup Panel (probability-recruited), self-administered web
response_options: Buckets as described by Gallup: daily / a few times a week / a few times a month / a few times a year / never
break_note: Verbatim stem unpublished — gap search documented 2026-07-07 (Indicator page, articles 691643/699689/701195/704225, Q4 topline PDF image-locked, Bentley PDF, Roper iPoll JS-gated). Gallup publishes definitions and buckets, never the stem.

publisher_definition: "Frequent AI users" are those who indicate they use AI at work a few times a week or more.
base_population: US adults 18+ working full or part time for organizations, Gallup Panel (probability-recruited), self-administered web
response_options: Buckets as described by Gallup: daily / a few times a week / a few times a month / a few times a year / never
break_note: Derived category from the same unpublished item as gallup-wf-total-users.

publisher_definition: Employees "saying they use AI daily" in their role (Gallup's published phrasing, e.g. "13% of employees now saying they use AI daily").
base_population: US adults 18+ working full or part time for organizations, Gallup Panel (probability-recruited), self-administered web
response_options: Buckets as described by Gallup: daily / a few times a week / a few times a month / a few times a year / never
break_note: Derived category from the same unpublished item as gallup-wf-total-users.

wording_verbatim: Has your organization integrated artificial intelligence (AI) technology?
publisher_definition: Reporting includes "all employees who at the time of survey said 'yes,' to the best of their knowledge, their organization had implemented AI technology or tools to improve organizational practices."
base_population: US adults 18+ working full or part time for organizations, Gallup Panel
response_options: Yes / No (+ Don't know from Q3 2025)
break_note: Gallup: "Starting in Q3 2025, Gallup added a 'don't know' option to this question … results from Q3 2025 and later for this question are not directly comparable with earlier measurements." First fielding date unpublished (pending).

wording_verbatim: In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)

response_options: Yes / No / Do not know
break_note: Census, Dec 2025: "Due to a level shift observed in conjunction with the new question wording, the decision was made to create a new time series for the AI questions, beginning with data released on December 4, 2025." Old series preserved as "AI Core Questions (Original)".

wording_verbatim: During the next six months, do you think this business will be using Artificial Intelligence (AI) in producing goods or services? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)
base_population: US employer businesses excluding farms, ~1.2M sample in six rotating biweekly panels
response_options: Yes / No / Do not know
break_note: Same Nov 2025 wording change and series cut as btos-current-v1.

wording_verbatim: In the last two weeks, did this business use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in any of its business functions? (Examples of AI: machine learning, natural language processing, virtual agents, voice recognition, etc.)

response_options: Yes / No / Do not know

response_options: Yes / No / Do not know

publisher_definition: Second AI supplement (Nov 17 2025–Feb 8 2026): current-use matrix (Q24) across 15 business functions, verbatim function list per NBER w35141 fn.12: "production of goods; provision of services, products, or merchandise; strategy and business development; finance and accounting; sales and marketing; customer service; research and development; information technology; human resources; public relations and communication; management and administration; sourcing, supply chains, and purchasing; quality management and control; distribution; and legal and compliance." wording_verbatim: Do you use Generative AI for your job? (Preceded by module definition: "Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence that creates text, images, audio, or video in response to prompts. Some examples of Generative AI include ChatGPT, Gemini, and Midjourney.")
base_population: Employed US adults 18–64 in the Real-Time Population Survey (online panel weighted to CPS/ACS benchmarks); genAI module gated by an awareness screener (module skipped by the ~25.5% who had not heard of genAI)

break_note: Pilot Jun 2024; full module from Aug 2024.
